title: Inline RFC 4103 T.140 to WebRTC data-channel gateway continuity
objective: Route the existing live SIP/RFC 4103 normal-profile media through an explicit gateway, forward the original RTP/RED datagrams unchanged to the SIP-side interpreter receiver, and carry the primary T.140 semantic stream through a real browser t140 data channel without duplicating RFC 2198 redundancy.

securityModel.rule: The gateway decodes SIP-side T.140 and re-originates content on a WebRTC data channel. Encryption may protect each leg, but this topology does not support an unqualified end-to-end encryption claim across the gateway.

runnableEvidence: JAIN SIP establishes the caller-to-interpreter dialog independently of browser state
RttSipProbe emits the existing deterministic direct text/t140 packet followed by RFC 2198 RED
the gateway preserves raw incoming datagrams before interpretation
the gateway forwards each incoming datagram unchanged to the existing Java RTT receiver
the gateway maps only the current primary T140block from each incoming packet onto the WebRTC data channel
the redundant H carried in the second RED packet remains recovery evidence and is not emitted as a duplicate character
a real Chromium RTCPeerConnection preserves ICE, DTLS, SCTP, candidate-pair, data-channel, and delivered-text evidence
Python independently parses the preserved RFC 4103/RFC 2198 inputs and compares their primary semantic stream with the browser-received text
requiredBeforeProven: repeatable routed execution through Sandia Wiretap or an equivalent controlled network substrate
network-induced loss/recovery in the routed substrate rather than sender-controlled omission
reverse WebRTC-to-RFC4103 direction using the same semantic reducer
at least one additional independent WebRTC implementation
production-representative VRS or gateway observations without provider-specific reducer branches
explicit review of media-termination and security evidence

doesNotEstablish: end-to-end encryption across the media-terminating gateway
